metadata.name: prediction_market
metadata.description: Prediction markets that settle from on-chain price history.

instructions.name: accept_authority
docs: Accepts a nomination.

instructions.name: adopt_params
docs: Applies a queued parameter change whose timelock has run out.

instructions.name: claim
docs: Burns a whole outcome position for the collateral it is owed and closes
the token account.

instructions.name: close_market
docs: Closes an emptied market and returns what rent can be returned.

instructions.name: collect_fee
docs: Pushes one of the three fee cuts to the party it belongs to.

accounts.name: destination
docs: Must be owned by whoever the chosen cut belongs to.

instructions.name: create_market
docs: Creates a market: mints, vault, spec, and the bond that pays its cranks.

accounts.name: mint
docs: Same account as `collateral.mint`; named separately so `has_one` can
bind them.

instructions.name: deposit
docs: Stakes collateral on a side and mints that side's outcome tokens 1:1.

accounts.name: side_mint
docs: The side being staked. Checked against the market in the handler so a
single context serves both sides.

instructions.name: initialize_config
docs: One-time setup. The deployer becomes the first authority and is
expected to hand it to a multisig immediately.

instructions.name: nominate_authority
docs: Nominates a new authority; it must accept before anything changes.

instructions.name: propose_params
docs: Queues a parameter change. It takes effect only after the timelock, and
only for markets created after that.

instructions.name: register_collateral
docs: Approves a collateral mint after checking it carries no extension that
would make the vault insolvent.

accounts.name: mint
docs: Classic SPL mints only.
`Account<Mint>` refuses anything the legacy Token program does not own,
which rules out Token-2022 entirely. That is deliberate for v1: a
transfer fee would make the vault structurally insolvent, since a
deposit of `x` arrives as `x - fee` while `x` outcome tokens are minted.
Admitting Token-2022 means screening every extension first.

instructions.name: register_feed
docs: Admits a price source to the registry, effective one timelock later.

accounts.name: pool
docs: `market_feeds`, which checks the discriminator. The pair's mints and
decimals are read out of it rather than taken as arguments: a
transposed pair or a wrong decimal count is a price normalised upside
down, discovered only when a market settles wrong.

accounts.name: observation_state
docs: that `pool_id` names the pool above; the pool must name it back.

instructions.name: register_pyth_feed
docs: Admits a Pyth instrument to the registry, effective one timelock later.

instructions.name: resolve
docs: Runs the predicate over the frozen prices and splits the pot.

instructions.name: set_paused
docs: Stops new markets from being created. Existing markets settle normally.

instructions.name: snapshot
docs: Freezes every declared feed's price for the settlement window.
Permissionless and paid from the bond. Separate from `resolve` so the
answer depends only on what was recorded, never on when the crank ran.

instructions.name: sweep_dust
docs: Sweeps rounding dust and unclaimed collateral once claiming has closed.

instructions.name: update_collateral
docs: Adjusts a collateral mint's floor, or withdraws it from new markets.

instructions.name: update_feed
docs: Updates a feed's attested depth, or disables it.

instructions.name: void
docs: Abandons a market that cannot settle honestly, refunding at par.

types.name: BoundaryRecord
docs: Both observations bounding the segment a window boundary falls in.
The pair, not just the nearer one: the interpolated cumulative depends on
the segment's slope, and a slope needs two points. Recording one would let
two different rings archive identical bytes and settle differently.

types.name: Collateral
docs: A collateral mint governance has approved.
Approval is explicit rather than implicit because a Token-2022 mint carrying
a transfer fee would make the vault structurally insolvent: a deposit of `x`
arrives as `x - fee` while `x` outcome tokens get minted. Transfer hooks and
permanent delegates are refused for the same reason.

fields.name: min_stake
docs: Smallest stake accepted, so that rent on the token accounts stays a
sane fraction of the bet.

types.name: Config
docs: Protocol-wide settings.

fields.name: authority
docs: Governance. Changes to it are two-step, so a typo cannot orphan the
protocol.

fields.name: paused
docs: Kill switch for new markets.
Exists because the price source is a program someone else can upgrade:
Raydium's CLMM sits behind a multisig, and if its account layout or its
accumulation rule ever changes, this stops new markets from being
created against it while existing ones settle out.

fields.name: pending_params
docs: Parameters waiting out the timelock, and when they become effective.

fields.name: timelock
docs: How long parameter and feed changes must wait, seconds.

fields.name: raydium_clmm_program
docs: The Raydium CLMM program whose pools this deployment reads.
Configured rather than hard-coded: it is an address that differs between
clusters and could be redeployed, and burying it in a constant would
make a wrong value a redeploy instead of a governance action.

fields.name: pyth_receiver_program
docs: The Pyth receiver program whose price accounts this deployment reads.

fields.name: markets_created
docs: Markets created so far, for reporting only.

fields.name: market_id
docs: Caller-chosen, so the market's address is known before signing.

fields.name: strike
docs: Value the predicate's score is compared against, Q64.64.

fields.name: ramp_bps
docs: Half-width of the settlement band, in basis points of the strike.

types.name: FeeRecipient
docs: Which of the three fee cuts is being collected.

types.name: Feed
docs: A price source governance has admitted.
Markets choose from the registry rather than naming pools directly: pool
creation is permissionless and has no liquidity floor, so a creator free to
pick sources can stand up two shallow pools and own the median of three.

fields.name: source_id
docs: Seeds this account. The ring's address for Raydium, the instrument id
for Pyth -- both 32 bytes, so nothing can be registered twice under two
names.

fields.name: pool
docs: Raydium only: the pool the ring belongs to.

fields.name: token0_mint
docs: Raydium only: the pair's mints, recorded for indexers.

fields.name: token0_decimals
docs: Raydium only: how the tick is normalised into a price. Pyth carries its
own exponent, so these are zero there.

fields.name: depth_quote
docs: Quote value that moves this pool's price by one percent, attested by
governance rather than measured. `PoolState.liquidity` is in-range `L`,
not depth: a $100 single-tick JIT position inflates it as much as $200k
spread normally. A trusted honest number beats an objective-looking one.

fields.name: effective_at
docs: When this feed becomes usable. Set one timelock into the future.

fields.name: label
docs: Human-readable pair label, for indexers.

types.name: FeedKind
docs: Both kinds exist because they answer to different assumptions: Raydium is
re-derivable by anyone from consensus state but needs a deep, busy pool;
Pyth covers far more instruments at the cost of trusting its publishers and
the guardians carrying their data.

types.name: FeedRef
docs: One price input of a market, naming a registry feed and how to read it.

fields.name: invert
docs: Read the pair the other way round: the price of `token1` in `token0`.
This is what lets one pool serve as either leg of a composed price, so
three genuinely independent estimates can be built out of pairs that
exist, instead of pretending three deep pools exist for every token.

types.name: Market
docs: The mutable half of a market.

fields.name: market_id
docs: Caller-chosen identifier, so the address is known before the
transaction is sent and two markets may share a spec.

fields.name: spec_hash
docs: Commits to the spec for good. Resolution checks it, so swapping the
spec account for another cannot change how a market settles.

fields.name: params
docs: Copied from `Config` at creation and never revisited.

fields.name: cap_per_side
docs: Per-side stake ceiling, in collateral base units.

fields.name: strike
docs: The value the predicate's score is compared against, Q64.64.

fields.name: ramp_bps
docs: Half-width of the settlement band, in basis points of the strike.
Applied by the program, never written into the predicate: a band buried
in bytecode could not be checked, so a creator could publish a step
function. Here every market has one, at least as wide as governance asks.

fields.name: staked_yes
docs: Authoritative stake counters.
Not the outcome mints' supplies: any holder can burn their own SPL
tokens through the Token program, which would shrink a supply while the
collateral stayed in the vault. Payout arithmetic anchored to supply
would then overpay whoever claimed last.

fields.name: share
docs: Fraction of the pot owed to YES, Q64.64, fixed at resolution.

fields.name: bond_lamports
docs: Refundable lamports held for the cranks.

types.name: MarketParams
docs: Governance parameters a market copies at creation.

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: Fee on the transferred amount, in basis points.

fields.name: feed_cap_bps
docs: Per-side stake cap as a fraction of the thinnest feed's attested depth.

fields.name: min_ramp_bps
docs: Narrowest settlement band a market may declare, in basis points.

fields.name: twap_window
docs: Averaging window, seconds.

fields.name: grace
docs: How long after settlement a snapshot may still be taken, seconds.

fields.name: skew
docs: Gap between the betting deadline and the window, seconds.

fields.name: max_segment
docs: Longest tolerated observation gap inside the window, seconds.

fields.name: min_observations
docs: Observations that must fall inside the window for a pool feed to count.

fields.name: creation_cooldown
docs: Delay between creating a market and opening it for bets, seconds.

fields.name: claim_window
docs: How long holders have to claim before dust is swept, seconds.

fields.name: pyth_window_tolerance
docs: Seconds either end of a Pyth window may differ from the requested one.

fields.name: max_confidence_bps
docs: Widest publisher disagreement a market will settle against, in basis
points of the price.

fields.name: max_down_slots_ratio
docs: Largest share of the window that may have fallen in missed slots, out

fields.name: keeper_reward
docs: Paid to each crank, in lamports, out of the creator's bond.

fields.name: creation_fee
docs: Non-refundable, in lamports. The bond alone is not an anti-spam measure:
a creator can crank their own market and get all of it back.

fields.name: share
docs: Fraction of the pot owed to YES, Q64.64.

types.name: MarketSpec
docs: The immutable half of a market: what it measures and how it decides.

types.name: MarketStatus
docs: Where a market is in its life. Mirrors `market_core::MarketState`.

types.name: ReadingRecord
docs: One feed's reading, in enough detail to reproduce it from archived state.

fields.name: probe_from
docs: A window the ring must be able to serve right now.
Registration proves the feed works by actually reading it, rather than
asserting that it will. A pool that cannot answer a probe today will not
answer a settlement tomorrow.

fields.name: feed_id
docs: The Pyth instrument identifier this feed quotes.

types.name: Snapshot
docs: Prices frozen at settlement, plus everything needed to re-derive them.
The raw observation indices and cumulatives are kept because the ring they
came from is overwritten within about twenty-five minutes on an active pool.
Without them a resolution could never be audited after the fact, which would
make "verifiable settlement" a claim rather than a property.

fields.name: feeds_hash
docs: Hash over every field below, so a snapshot can be quoted compactly.

fields.name: prices
docs: Q64.64 prices, in the order the spec declares its feeds.

types.name: SourceRecord
docs: Everything needed to re-derive one reading, whatever produced it.
Archived differently because they are verifiable differently: a Raydium
reading is reproduced from Solana's own history, so the raw pair is what
matters, while a Pyth account was transient and cannot be reproduced at all —
so what is kept is the assertion believed and the tests it passed.

types.name: VoidCause
docs: Why a market was abandoned. Mirrors `market_core::VoidReason`.

constants.name: MIN_MARKET_FEEDS
docs: Three, so a median survives one source being captured. Raising it costs
coverage; lowering it costs the median its point.
`#[constant]` puts it in the IDL, which is where the client reads it from —
a second copy in the front end would drift the first time this changes.
